A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. The main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A-G support reliable comparison, including matching retained content across table renumbering and pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-identification experiments, conversational identification results, and case studies of cooperation, preference alignment and jailbreaking.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds option-order robustness and granular identity-identification experiments in Appendix C.3.

M1.justification: The identifier-target framework, dimension-focused prompting, conversational inference and three case-study procedures remain unchanged. Appendix C.3 extends evaluation of the existing framework.

E1.justification: v2 extends identification beyond model families to exact model names and parameter-size categories, using Claude 3.7 Sonnet and four targets on HumanEval. This is a narrow task extension; the existing datasets and other evaluated tasks are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged, including the identity-hidden comparisons. The new diagnostics reuse existing models and introduce evaluation conditions rather than competing methods.

E3.justification: Appendix C.3 adds per-query randomization of family-to-option-letter assignments with four identifier models. The granular experiment uses one identifier and four targets selected as preceding its knowledge cutoff. Existing evaluation protocols and settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Two focused analyses are added: a fixed-versus-randomized option-order control testing positional bias, and a granularity analysis testing recognition of model names and sizes. Existing feature, reasoning-capability, knowledge-cutoff, conversational and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 5 retains 95% confidence intervals over three independent runs, and Appendix D retains 20 trial conversations per identifier-target pair. The new analyses introduce no additional uncertainty reporting, run counts, seeds or significance tests.

E6.justification: New Table 4 adds randomized-order results: in-family F1 is 0.36 versus fixed-order 0.34 for GPT, and 0.41 versus 0.42 for Claude. Table 5 reports exact-name accuracies of 0-26% and 75% size-category accuracy for Haiku. Previously reported results, including Figure 5's means and confidence intervals, are unchanged.

T1.justification: No new theoretical assumptions, propositions, proofs or derivations are introduced. The existing pass@k and win-lose-ratio formulas remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and substantive conclusion retain the same contributions: family identification, stronger in-family recognition, and beneficial or risky identity-dependent adaptation. The added concluding research question does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix C.3 newly interprets option-order stability as evidence against positional-bias explanations and granular results as showing limited awareness beyond model families. The conclusion adds the question of preserving distinctive model characteristics versus standardizing them to prevent identity inference. The existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 provides limited implementation information for the added diagnostics, including named model subsets, per-query option shuffling and size bins of <7B, 7B-13B, 13B-70B and >70B. Existing prompt templates, hyperparameters and code/data access information are retained; granular prompts and size-label ground truth are not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds Robinson and Wingate (2023) and Zheng et al. (2024) on multiple-choice behavior to motivate the positional-bias control. The related-work section and central novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized edits add descriptive subheadings and analysis paragraphs in Appendix C.3, a future-research sentence in the conclusion, and small wording and author-contact changes. The overall narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 4-5 and renumbers the former Tables 4-9 as Tables 6-11. Figure 5 is restyled with revised labels and a 0-100 accuracy axis replacing 0-1, preserving the plotted results. Figure 2's caption clarifies aggregation and metrics, and Figure 1 corrects a typo.

improvement.justification: The new option-order control addresses an untested confound in v1, while the granular experiment makes limits of identity recognition more concrete. These provide a limited net improvement in validation. The gains are constrained by missing uncertainty estimates and underdocumented size-accuracy claims: Table 2 still lists proprietary model parameter counts as unknown.
